title: Add JSONSchema strict mode and OpenAI-compatible response_format handling
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: add first-class JSON Schema support for structured output (response_format) with a strict validation mode and OpenAI-compatible response_format parsing. This PR implements server-side schema validation, clearer validation error messages, and best-effort enforcement during streaming. It also adds compatibility parsing for OpenAI-style response_format payloads and wires the feature through the API surface and SDKs.

Changes: implements a lightweight validation pipeline that runs a relaxed validation pass during streaming (so partial responses can be surfaced) and a final strict validation pass post-generation when strict=true. Adds new error codes (INVALID_SCHEMA, RESPONSE_VALIDATION_FAILED, STREAM_VALIDATION_WARNING) and maps those to HTTP 400/422 appropriately. Introduces OpenAI-compatible response_format parsing that accepts both the legacy "response_format": {"type":"json_schema", ...} and the newer Redwood form, with migration shims.

Checklist:
- [x] core validation engine (inference/runtime)
- [x] OpenAI-compatible response_format parser and normalization
- [x] API layer changes: request parsing, error mapping, telemetry for validation failures
- [x] SDK changes: Python + TypeScript typed helpers and examples
- [x] end-to-end tests including streaming + strict mode regression tests
- [x] docs and changelog entries
- [x] performance tests to ensure tail latency impact is <5% in typical workloads

Testing: added unit tests for schema parsing, property coercion, and error message formatting. Added e2e test that exercises streaming validation (ensures streaming continues with warning logs and final strict failure when appropriate). CI had an intermittent lint failure which was fixed in the second commit; all checks passing on merge.

Backward compatibility & migration: default behavior remains permissive (strict=false). Existing customers who rely on permissive parsing are unaffected. The OpenAI compatibility shim tolerates older shapes of response_format; customers can opt-in to strict mode via query param or request body flag (response_format.strict=true).

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to the validation cost paths (validate_streaming_prefix and final_strict_validate) and the SDK helper surface; the TypeScript helper uses a small runtime to validate and narrow responses for callers using the OpenAI compat helper.
commits_summary: feat(runtime): add JSONSchema validation pipeline with streaming-safe prefix checks
feat(api): parse OpenAI-compatible response_format and normalize schema payloads
fix(sdk): expose response_format helpers in python/typescript SDKs
test: add unit and e2e tests for streaming + strict mode
docs: update structured-output docs and changelog

release_notes: Adds JSON Schema structured-output support with a new strict validation mode (opt-in). Includes OpenAI-compatible response_format parsing and improved validation error messages. Default behavior remains permissive; opt-in strict=true will enforce schema validity and return clear 4xx errors when responses do not conform. SDK helpers and docs updated.
